discoveries.headline: Raoul Pal's latest, picked by Lisa
discoveries.why: Lisa picked Raoul Pal's latest post on X for today, so you can hear his view straight from the source. Pal is a well-followed voice on markets and crypto, and his posts are a window into how one macro thinker sees the moment. Read it as one voice among many. Education, not advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: Raoul Pal (@RaoulGMI) · chosen by Lisa Wade

discoveries.headline: Mongolia's president says he will step down
discoveries.why: Mongolia's President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa has said he will resign after a member of his own party accused him of taking US$25 million linked to a railway contract awarded in 2019 without a competitive tender. Two senior officials named in the claims said they would go too, and the resignation takes effect only if parliament accepts it. A short, clear report on a political shake-up in a country that rarely makes our news.

discoveries.headline: A rescued kitten turns out to be a new wild cat
discoveries.why: An orphan kitten handed in to a Bolivian wildlife refuge in 2017 has grown up to be a whole new species, Leopardus tilcayo, described as the first new wild cat in more than 100 years. Genome studies show its line split from its closest relatives about 1.43 million years ago, and biologist Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz says only one is known in captivity. A lovely reminder of how much of the wild we still haven't met.
discoveries.credit: Photos: Fernando Faciole / National Geographic; Botánica Films / Emi Kondo

discoveries.headline: Mindfulness 101 with Jon Kabat-Zinn
discoveries.why: Jon Kabat-Zinn, who began Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction more than 40 years ago, explains how to start: paying attention, on purpose, in the present moment, without judging. He clears up the biggest myth, that you're meant to make your mind blank, and reminds us that meditation is a way of being, not a doing. Eighteen calm minutes for the commute, to ease the rush before the day takes off.
discoveries.meta_credit: Life Kit · Shereen Marisol Meraji with Jon Kabat-Zinn

discoveries.headline: Waleed Aly on finding meaning in the chaos
discoveries.why: Waleed Aly asks how we come to grips with a world that feels like it's coming apart, and how to tell what is truly new in this moment from what isn't. He joins Conversations to talk about his book Reasoning with Chaos, which grew from his columns for Melbourne's The Age. A thoughtful hour for the commute, and it leaves ABC listen on 30 November.
discoveries.meta_credit: Conversations · Richard Fidler and Sarah Kanowski · Waleed Aly

discoveries.headline: Atong Atem's first major solo show
discoveries.why: Passage: The Art of Atong Atem at NGV Australia celebrates the Melbourne-based South Sudanese photographer, who turns her own body into a canvas of textiles, paint and symbolic objects. Her portraits draw on African studio photography, family archives, Catholic imagery and science fiction, and honour Dinka Bor myths and traditions. Free entry at Fed Square until 14 June 2027.
discoveries.meta_credit: NGV · The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia

discoveries.headline: What the sour taste does, in Ayurveda
discoveries.why: Ayurvedic practitioner Molly McConnell explains why Ayurveda sees the sour taste as warming and moistening, and most balancing for vata, while too much may stir up pitta or kapha. She is honest that the science is thin so far, and her suggestion is simple: add a few citrus fruits, tomatoes or pickled vegetables to your shopping, and skip the sour lollies. General information, not medical advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: Banyan Botanicals · Molly McConnell, CAP, ERYT

discoveries.headline: A 25-minute flow for beginners
discoveries.why: Yoga teacher Natasha Lee leads a 25-minute beginner flow in eight parts, from cat-cow and sun salutations to tree pose, warriors and a closing savasana. The article lists every pose in order, with her full video to follow along. A gentle way to build a morning ritual if you're new to the mat.
discoveries.meta_credit: Tom's Guide · Mollie Davies, with yoga teacher Natasha Lee

discoveries.headline: Why people who lift live longer
discoveries.why: A study following nearly 150,000 US health professionals for up to 30 years linked 90 to 120 minutes of strength training a week to about a 13% lower risk of dying from any cause. Exercise physiologist Jack McNamara walks through the findings, including the bigger benefit when lifting was paired with aerobic exercise, and is clear that the study was observational. A good nudge to make lifting part of your week.
discoveries.meta_credit: 1News · Jack McNamara, University of East London (republished from The Conversation)
